title: Review of the CIPS gene-selection negative on fresh seed 7: the normal-catalysis mutants are not favoured over the 10%-deficient ancestors (mutant share 0.40 with the trait vs 0.53 in the twin; mutant/ancestor births per body 0.094/0.046 vs 0.106/0.051), the washed population holds at 8-14 bodies, and the trait arm again carries ~2 fewer bodies
summary: sel.py, world.py, ana.py and rates.py copied unchanged; seed 7; ancestors g2 (inoc_kind 2) with a2 -0.1 and the a2 0 twin with the same swap (every 100 t) and washout (every 1000 t from t=6000) streams; T=16000 (the finding ran 25000). ana.py: mutant (g1) share over t=11000-16000 0.40 (trait) vs 0.53 (twin), ending 5 g1 : 7 g2 and 7 : 7; 7 and 11 swap hits, 10 removals each. rates.py from t=6000: per-capita births g1/g2 0.094/0.046 (trait) and 0.106/0.051 (twin), so the mutant-to-ancestor ratio is the same with and without the deficit. Bodies from t=6000: mean 10.8 (8-13) with the trait, 12.7 (11-14) in the twin. labkit re-run of the a2 -0.1 world on seed 7 (192^2, T=12000): 5 persistent splits, generation 1, 0 merges.

observations.H: rates_s7.txt and ana_s7.png: mutant share 0.40 (trait) vs 0.53 (twin) over the last 5000 t; mutant/ancestor births per body 0.094/0.046 vs 0.106/0.051: a 10% catalysis deficit is not selected against under washout on seed 7

seeds_run.result: negative for selection reproduced; steady washed population and the trait arm's 1-2 body deficit reproduced

controls_run.H: a2 0 twin with the same swap and washout streams (sel2_s7_a0.0.json)

verdicts.limitation: One seed, T=16000 instead of 25000, and only 7-9 births per arm after t=6000, so the rates are noisy. I did not re-run the no-washout assay. 'Supported' means the negative result replicates.
